subject: Throughput regression: coordinated action plan and customer comms
messages:
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] us-west throughput regression — initial alert

Team,

We started seeing a sustained throughput drop in us-west-prod at ~08:45 PST (14:45 UTC). Key points:
- Throughput down ~45% vs baseline across the inference fleet serving gpt-small variants.
- P99 latency increased from ~220ms to ~1.1s; p50 only shifted ~80ms.
- No ongoing deploys reported via CI in the 30m window prior to the spike.

Initial observations from the metrics: we see a sharp rise in NVMe I/O wait on nodes handling prefix cache population, and a correlated jump in kernel scheduling on a subset of GPU hosts (hosts: usw-prod-batch-01..06). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cluster/throughput?panelId=9

Immediate asks:
1) Neha/Jonas: start triage (heap/profile + strace on one host), can we isolate whether this is infra or runtime (KV cache eviction loop)?
2) Product (Stephanie): advise on customer message cadence and whether to suggest a conservative mitigation (feature flag toggle / rolling restart) vs rollback.
3) Sales (Ava/Marissa): prepare a short, transparent comm for impacted customers — BrightFrame has reported timeouts.

Attaching current perf graphs + timeline. I'll start a PagerDuty incident (PD#INC-7836).

-Marcus

Attachments: perf-graphs-20261115.png (png)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] us-west throughput regression — initial alert

Thanks Marcus — good catch. Quick clarifying questions:
- Is the scope limited to gpt-small pools or are we seeing cross-model impact?
- Any downstream 5xx spikes from edge proxies?

My recommendation for now:
1) If we can flip a config flag (disable auto-shard / cache-prefetch) with minimal risk, do that immediately as a mitigation.
2) If mitigation doesn't show measurable improvement within 30 minutes, prepare an emergency rollback of the last runtime change and notify legal/finance for potential SLAs.
3) Sales should send a short notice to impacted customers offering an ETA and a single point of contact. Keep commitments conservative.

Product ask (for roadmap / follow-up): prioritize a guardrail that prevents aggressive cache evictions and introduce a canary for auto-shard changes — open a ticket to track.

-Stephanie

(Adding: please thread any customer replies into this thread so we have a single source of truth.)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] us-west throughput regression — triage update

Quick update from SRE triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: a regression in the 'auto-shard' logic introduced a tight loop that significantly increased async disk reads leading to NVMe saturation on affected hosts. The loop triggers during concurrent cold-prefix population.
- Evidence: iostat /proc/diskstats shows 4-6x read amplification on nodes in the affected hostset; kernel perf shows dominant time in io_submit wait states.

Mitigation applied at 09:20 PST: toggled runtime flag disable_auto_shard=true on the affected rolling subset (hosts 01-03 first wave). Observed partial recovery within 5 minutes on wave 1.

Planned next steps (timeline):
- 09:25–09:50: finish rolling toggle across all affected hosts (expected 25 m).
- 09:50: verify global p99 and throughput metrics; if improvement >= 30% vs peak regression, we continue and monitor.
- If no sufficient improvement, we will stage a rollback of last runtime artifact (requires coordination with Deploy) — estimate 45 minutes.

Attaching hotfix diff for the guardrail we'll propose for the PR (hotfix-diff.patch).

-Neha (SRE)

Attachments: hotfix-diff.patch (text)

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Alice Park <alice@brightframe.com>, BrightFrame Ops <ops@brightframe.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Incident: brief update on degraded throughput affecting some requests (US-West)

Hi Alice / BrightFrame Ops,

I wanted to reach out with a short update — our engineering team detected an infrastructure-level issue affecting a subset of requests in US-West earlier this morning. You may have seen elevated latency or intermittent timeouts.

What happened (brief):
- We observed a sudden drop in throughput and higher p99 latency starting ~08:45 PST. Our SREs traced the cause to a runtime behavior that increased disk I/O on some inference hosts.

Immediate impact:
- Some inference requests for models on the gpt-small pool may have experienced timeouts or slower responses.

What we're doing now:
- SREs have toggled a mitigation flag and are performing a rolling rollout across affected hosts. Early waves showed partial recovery and we expect the action to complete within ~25–30 minutes.
- We will follow up with a post-incident summary and a timeline once the situation is stable.

Customer ask / ETA:
- We expect visible improvement for all of your traffic by ~10:00 PST. If you are still seeing issues after 10:15 PST please reply to this thread and we'll escalate immediately.

Point of contact: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwood.com) is handling the incident response; I'm copied on updates.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll share the incident timeline and remediation plan shortly.

Thanks for your patience,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-timeline-20261115.txt (text)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident: brief update on degraded throughput affecting some requests (US-West)

Status update:
- Rolling toggle completed across affected hosts at 09:52 PST.
- Post-toggle metrics: throughput recovered ~38% vs lowest point, p99 reduced to ~280ms (from 1.1s).
- No additional error-rate spikes observed at the proxy layer.

Action items:
- Product (Stephanie): please open a SUP ticket to track the follow-up guardrail and prioritization for next sprint (SUP-2345).
- SRE (Neha/Jonas): collect the full host-level traces & produce a short RCA draft by EOD.
- Sales (Ava/Marissa): offer BrightFrame a 1:1 postmortem and consider a service credit if their SLO was breached — keep legal/finance in the loop.

We'll keep monitoring for the next 4 hours. Good triage work from the SRE team.

-Marcus

PD incident: INC-7836

Cc: BrightFrame Ops <ops@brightframe.com>
